note: Before defranceski.com is switched off, everything on it was captured, compared against this archive page by page, and either matched to where it already lives here or written down as something new. This is that reckoning. It is published rather than kept in a notebook so that anyone who remembers the old site can see what became of each part of it.

rows.lab: Both Google MyMaps, exported as KML
rows.text: «Defranceski Family» — the primary map, 1,345 placemarks in ten layers — and «Old Defranceski Family», 93 placemarks. Exported as KML while they were still live and archived. This was the single most urgent thing on the site: the maps are David's own research, not published anywhere else, and a MyMap dies with the Google account that holds it.

rows.lab: What is in the primary map
rows.text: «Family Search Books Available», 1,022 pins — every Croatian place with a FamilySearch book, which is a research instrument in its own right. «My Known Defranceski Family», 37. «Istra Lines of Defranceschi», 42. «Bepo and Nana De Franceschi», 21 — the Omiš–Imotski narrative. «Italian Lines», 90. «High Level of Emigration from Here», 44. «German Defranceski's», 14. «Early Line in Rijeka», 4. «Random Markers», 6. And an untitled layer of 75.

covered.heading: Page by page: what the old site said, and where it is now
rows: Home — the purpose, and the six hotspots
Seget, Gologorica, Ližnjan, Omiš, Mione, Corsica, and onward to Koper, Crete, Johannesburg, Germany, the United States and Australia.

Every one of those is a page or a section here. Ližnjan is now third of eighteen towns in the record sweep and has its own man in Ante Defrančeski; Corsica is on the roadmap; Crete is the Seget tradition, argued against on the Carnia page.
Family Trees — the linear chart
Giovanni 1750–1829 · Giovanni 1787–1846 · Antonio 1825–1894 · Josip 1863–1951 · Antonio 1890–1943 · Ivan 1925–1995 · Ivan · David.

Carried across exactly, and every one of those dates is now on the Direct Line page — most of them with the register page behind them rather than the chart. Nothing was lost and a good deal was added.
The People

Carlo, Camillo, Andrea and Titian, Girolamo, Alessandro OP, Francesco the painter, Francesco the printer, Domenico, Mariano, Carlo Francesco the composer, the two Napoleonic Defrance / Franceschi-Delonne.

All on the Namesakes page, most now with fuller lives and every one labelled as kin or not kin. Two remain owed: Andrea and Titian, and Francesco the painter — both still open, both listed on the roadmap.

The Story · The Name
The spellings: Franceschi, De Franceschi, Franceschini, Defrančeski, Defranceschi, Dei Francesci, de Franceschi.

The Name page carries all of these and more, with counts. «Defrančeski» is now evidenced three times in print and in five Zagreb graves; «Franceschini» and «Dei Francesci» are noted as variants this archive has not found in its own records.

newfound.heading: And four things on the old site that this archive did not have
newfound.lead: The comparison was supposed to be a formality. It was not.

rows.lab: «Franceschi dalle Rose» — chased, and it is almost certainly a confusion
rows.text: The pin read «Franceschi dalle Rose Move 1040 to Venice», with Ravenna and the Giudecca beside it. Searched: the form does not exist in the literature. What does exist, and matches the pin exactly, is the **Donà dalle Rose** — a Venetian noble house whose own origin story runs from Romagna and Altinum, which is to say Ravenna, whose «dalle Rose» is the main surviving branch, and which gave Venice two Doges. «Dalle Rose» is their byname, not this family's. The likeliest reading is that a nobiliary source was misfiled at some point and the two ran together. It is recorded here so that it does not get repeated: this archive can find no Franceschi dalle Rose anywhere.

rows.lab: A German branch route this archive had no idea about
rows.text: The «German Defranceski's» layer runs Ližnjan → Monheim, with «Grga dies in Zagreb», and separately «Petar Moves to Metzingen». Metzingen is four kilometres from Pfullingen, which is where the family's own wartime papers are from. Ližnjan is the third-largest cluster in the record sweep. Neither Grga nor the Monheim line appears anywhere in this archive.

rows.lab: The Veneto emigration hotspots, and São Paulo
rows.text: A layer of forty-four pins — Castelnuovo, Pederobba, Cornedo Vicentino, Castelgomberto, Scorzè, Moniego — all in the Veneto, all marked as places of heavy emigration, ending at «State of São Paulo». This archive's Diaspora page has the Brazilian cluster as the largest of all and has never had a departure region for it. Here is a candidate one.

rows.lab: The Dalmatian narrative, laid out as a route
rows.text: Ravenna → Venice 1040 → Giudecca → Niccolò to Zadar in the 1300s → Tomasso to Omiš → Francesca de Franceschi from Venice to Omiš in the 1500s → Zuane to Imotski → Antonio to Proložac → Antonia to Trsat → Pisak and Vruja. Most of it this archive now holds independently and in more detail. Two names in it are new: Tomasso, and Francesca de Franceschi of the 1500s.

verdict: On the evidence of a page-by-page comparison, defranceski.com can be switched off without losing anything — provided the two MyMaps are either kept alive or left as the archived KML, which they now are. Everything else it carried is either here already, in better condition, or is written down above as something still to do.
